text:
anya: heads up — onboarding GAU-xxl-v2 for hosted. quick preflight: weights are in s3://redwood-models/gau-xxl-v2/2026-03-01/, tokenizer.json looks different from our usual sentencepiece. can folks sanity-check memory footprint and kv cache format before i flip the config?

mike: thanks. do we have the model max_seq_len? that will drive kv cache size.

anya: model config claims max_seq_len: 131072 but noticed tokenizer truncates at 65536 tokens during conversion. not sure which is authoritative.

jess: if tokenizer is truncating at 65k then effective max ctx is 65k unless we swap tokenizer. need to confirm tokenization on a long document. can you share a minimal repro?

anya: here's a quick check i ran locally:
```bash
echo "$(yes 'hello world' | head -n 100000)" > big.txt
python tools/tokenize.py --model s3://redwood-models/gau-xxl-v2/tokenizer.json big.txt | wc -l
```
result: 65536 tokens.

lee: hmm. tokenizer format is the new json-bpe variant. our kvcache serialization expects kv-shard ordering (seq-major) vs the model runtime which uses interleaved kv. mismatch could blow up memory usage.

sam: infra-bot reports current hosted runtime uses kv-format: "interleaved-v2" for this hostpool. if runtime expects interleaved and our kvcache dump is seq-major, we'll pay a conversion cost + temp memory. how big is the KV per token for GAU-xxl-v2?

mike: rough numbers: GAU-xxl-v2, 64-heads, head-dim 128 => key+value per token ~ (64*128*2)*2 bytes per fp16 ~ 32768 bytes? wait calc: 64*128=8192, *2 (k+v)=16384 floats, *2 bytes (fp16)=32768 bytes per token. so 32KB/token => 65k * 32KB ~= 2.08GB just for kv at 65k. but we also need model activations and temp buffers. OOM risk high on 80GB GPU if batching >1.

jess: good breakdown. add attention cache overhead and per-layer int buffers — plan for ~2.6-3GB for kvcache at 65k for single request. with batching we multiply.

anya: ok — next steps I think: (1) pin max_ctx in model config to 65536 to match tokenizer, (2) add kvcache-format: "interleaved-v2" to model manifest, (3) add a pre-deploy check that validates tokenization length vs declared max_ctx and warns, (4) flag single-request memory calc in the console. any objections?

lee: +1 on pinning. we should also include a fallback route: if OOM risk predicted for a request (based on tokens * per-token-kv), route to smaller variant or stream with truncation.

sam: i'll add a quick diagnostic to the console that estimates kvcache bytes given model params and declared max_ctx. PR in infra-tools coming.

jess: i'll open a PR to update the model manifest and manifest validator with the tokenizer check. assigning to @mike for code review. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-models/pull/312

mike: will review today. also suggest we add a runtime metric telemetry tag for "kv_format_mismatch" so ops can alert when conversion occurs.

infra-bot: deploy-check — manifest schema v2 validated. kvcache-format field present. tokenization-test: failed on sample long-doc (65536 vs declared 131072) — see logs: https://logs.redwood/inference/1749812345

anya: thanks infra-bot — i'll update the manifest to set max_ctx=65536 and update weights manifest path to s3://redwood-models/gau-xxl-v2/2026-03-01/weights/ (was missing shard-idx in earlier draft).

sam: tagging in oncall @lee for any infra changes. Lee, can you estimate memory headroom on 80GB nodes if we keep max_ctx 65k?

lee: for single request: ~3.2GB kvcache + 20-30GB model activations + model params in GPU memory (~40GB for gaus?), realistic headroom <10GB. with batching 2 we're toast. need to restrict concurrent large-ctx requests per node and enforce per-route concurrency=1.

anya: noted. i'll add per-model concurrency default to 1 for gaus and include a gating flag in rollout to dedicated that checks node capacity.

jess: also add a small note in docs: "Models with effective ctx > 32k should be reviewed by infra before enabling burst autoscale".

mike: LGTM. i'll land review after test pass.

anya: thanks team — i'll push the manifest update and link PRs here. ping me with any regressions. :thumbsup:
